answer: A durable defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, non-transferable work history: every completed job leaves a verifiable thread of signed receipts, references and client ratings that cannot be bought in bulk. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, with tiny limits, and only earns higher limits slowly, like yarrow spreading one rooted shoot at a time. Forging a thousand fake agents then means paying for a thousand slow histories, which costs more than any single scam can recover.
